benchmark_type_evidence: we introduce M3Exam, a novel benchmark sourced from real and official human exam questions for evaluating LLMs in a multilingual, multimodal, and multilevel context
brief_description: M3Exam is a benchmark of 12,317 multiple-choice questions sourced from real official human exams in 9 languages across 3 educational levels (primary, middle, high school), covering 4 subject categories (language, math, social science, natural science), with approximately 23% of questions requiring image processing.

datasets.annotation_method: Native speakers from each country collected official exam papers; annotators performed OCR, checked text, fixed errors, transformed into unified format with multiple rounds of quality checks

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: Alibaba DAMO Academy data management and annotation team, with annotators from various linguistic and cultural backgrounds
data_creator_info.evidence: We extend our gratitude to the data management and annotation team at Alibaba DAMO Academy, particularly Yanyan Zheng, Tantong Champaiboon, Nguyen Ngoc Yen Nhi, and Andila Putri Susanti. Their kind assistance in coordinating the annotators, processing the data, and conducting quality checks has been important to our work. We would also like to thank the annotators from various linguistic and cultural backgrounds who collaborated to contribute to this unique multilingual dataset.

datasets.notes: Questions sourced from real official human exams (435 exam papers from 9 countries). 12,317 total questions: 9,501 text-only and 2,816 requiring images. Covers 3 educational levels (low/primary, mid/middle school, high/high school) and 4 subject categories (language, math, social science, natural science). Swahili and Javanese only have low and mid levels. Released under CC BY-NC-SA License.

translated.evidence: collecting real-world natural data of different languages instead of translating from English data is of great importance, as culture and world knowledge are deeply rooted in authentic data; we engage native speakers from each of the selected countries to collect official exam papers along with their answers at the end of each educational level

native_annotators.evidence: we engage native speakers from each of the selected countries to collect official exam papers along with their answers; We would also like to thank the annotators from various linguistic and cultural backgrounds who collaborated to contribute to this unique multilingual dataset.

culturally_grounded.evidence: by gathering questions from official exams across multiple countries, the benchmark contains natural multilingual questions in different languages, which retain the social-cultural diversity of knowledge that may be essential for problem-solving; some existing multilingual benchmarks...that were created by translating original English datasets have been found to introduce an English-centric bias...This shows the importance of sourcing real data from various languages to represent their native cultural background

M3Exam.annotation_quality_notes: Multiple rounds of quality checks were conducted. Annotators checked OCR text, fixed errors, separated question text from answer options, input correct answers, included contextual background information, converted special formats (equations to LaTeX, bold text), and annotated image placeholders.

datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: collecting real-world natural data of different languages instead of translating from English data is of great importance; we engage native speakers from each of the selected countries to collect official exam papers

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: The paper explicitly contrasts with translated benchmarks: 'some existing multilingual benchmarks of traditional NLP tasks that were created by translating original English datasets have been found to introduce an English-centric bias.' M3Exam sources questions from real exams in each country's language.

details.M3Exam: Questions sourced from official national exams in 9 countries (US, China, Italy, Brazil, Vietnam, Thailand, Kenya, South Africa, Indonesia), retaining social-cultural diversity and requiring country-specific knowledge. Example: Thai questions require knowledge of Thai geography; Chinese questions test Chinese historical knowledge.

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: we engage native speakers from each of the selected countries to collect official exam papers along with their answers; We would also like to thank the annotators from various linguistic and cultural backgrounds who collaborated to contribute to this unique multilingual dataset.

annotator_workforce.evidence: We extend our gratitude to the data management and annotation team at Alibaba DAMO Academy, particularly Yanyan Zheng, Tantong Champaiboon, Nguyen Ngoc Yen Nhi, and Andila Putri Susanti. Their kind assistance in coordinating the annotators, processing the data, and conducting quality checks has been important to our work.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The benchmark was explicitly designed to avoid English-centricity. Questions are sourced from real exams in each country's native language. The paper notes: 'some existing multilingual benchmarks...that were created by translating original English datasets have been found to introduce an English-centric bias. This bias arises because the translation process...does not always capture culturally specific or unique concepts present in the target languages.' However, English is one of the 9 languages and has the most questions (2,738 total).

geographic_representation.evidence: we select 9 languages including English (from the US), Chinese (from China), Italian (from Italy), Portuguese (from Brazil), Vietnamese (from Vietnam), Thai (from Thailand), Swahili (from Kenya), Afrikaans (from South Africa), and Javanese (from Indonesia). This selection is mainly driven by language and cultural diversity, with the aim of covering different language families, languages with varying levels of resources, written scripts, and their major spoken countries.
